Files are added to the session separately and become a previewable site when the session is finalized. Original image files are stored as given, without resizing. tools.name: upload_site_file
tools.description: Saves one text file of the website (html, css, js, svg, json) into an open session, with encoding 'utf8'. Logos, icons and illustrations work well as SVG. base64 is accepted for tiny binary files only (a few KB).

tools.name: upload_file_chunk
tools.description: Saves a binary file into an open session in pieces, for files that can only be supplied as text. The file's base64 text is split into consecutive pieces of at most 12000 characters, each sent with chunk_index 0..total_chunks-1 (any order). When the last piece arrives the file is assembled and saved.

tools.name: import_file_from_url
tools.description: Has the server download a file (image, font, a .zip of a whole site) from a public https URL into an open session, so the file's bytes do not need to be passed through the chat. Private and localhost addresses are not accepted. If path ends in .zip the archive is unpacked into the site root.

tools.name: import_attached_file
tools.description: Saves a file the user attached to the chat (for example their logo or a photo) into the website. Pass the attached file as `file` and say where it goes with `path`, e.g. images/logo.png. If `path` is omitted it is saved as images/<original file name>. tools.description: Returns a short-lived HTTP upload endpoint (valid 15 minutes) for one publish session, plus a ready curl command. tools.name: list_session_files
tools.description: Lists the files received so far for a session (from tool uploads and the browser upload page).

tools.name: finalize_upload
tools.description: Checks the uploaded site and creates a temporary preview URL (valid for 48 hours) plus a link the site owner uses to create an account and publish. tools.name: get_site_preview
tools.description: Returns a fresh temporary preview URL for the most recent version uploaded in a finalized session.

tools.name: publish_site
tools.description: Checks where a finalized site is in the publishing process and what has to happen next. tools.name: list_my_sites
tools.description: Lists the websites that belong to the signed-in customer, with status, live address and number of versions.

tools.name: get_site
tools.description: Returns one of the signed-in customer's sites with its list of versions (id, upload time, size, and which one is live).

tools.name: update_site
tools.description: Starts an update session for one of the signed-in customer's existing sites. The session begins as a copy of the files that are live now, so only changed or new files need to be added to it. tools.name: read_session_file
tools.description: Returns the text of one file in an open session (html, css, js, svg, json up to 200 KB). Binary files such as images are reported by name and size only.

tools.name: rollback_site
tools.description: Makes an earlier version of the signed-in customer's site live again. Without deployment_id it returns to the previous version. Version ids are shown with the site's details.

tools.name: upload_site_files
tools.description: Saves several text files of the website into an open session in one call (html, css, js, svg, json), with the same rules as saving a single file.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: upload_site_file, import_file_from_url, get_site_preview, read_session_file, upload_site_files, create_site_from_files, read_site_file · Private data: create_publish_session, upload_site_file, upload_file_chunk, import_file_from_url, import_attached_file, request_upload_link, list_session_files, finalize_upload, update_site, read_session_file, upload_site_files, create_site_from_files, update_site_files, read_site_file · Public sink: create_publish_session, upload_site_file, upload_file_chunk, request_upload_link, list_session_files, finalize_upload, publish_site, get_site, upload_site_files, create_site_from_files, update_site_files.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: upload_site_file, import_file_from_url, get_site_preview, read_session_file, upload_site_files, create_site_from_files, read_site_file · Private data: create_publish_session, upload_site_file, upload_file_chunk, import_file_from_url, import_attached_file, request_upload_link, list_session_files, finalize_upload, update_site, read_session_file, upload_site_files, create_site_from_files, update_site_files, read_site_file · Public sink: create_publish_session, upload_site_file, upload_file_chunk, request_upload_link, list_session_files, finalize_upload, publish_site, get_site, upload_site_files, create_site_from_files, update_site_files

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_site_guidance" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
